description:
`Defk.Bench` writes the `DEFK_RESULT` map twice (`check_only/1` ~L290 and `print/2` ~L685, bench.ex); dev/ reads it by 31 distinct string keys across examples.ex (`parse_results/1`, `judge/5`, `verdict_of/3`), scoreboard.ex (18 key reads), snapshot.ex, tables.ex and the defk.examples task. The verdict order and marks are written twice (`Scoreboard.verdict_rank/verdict_mark` ~L173-183, `Tables.rank/mark` ~L343-353); the bands are a third place (Bench ~L109-113). Following "run one example and record its verdict" opens seven files, which are the hot files of the last 80 commits.

Settled shape (grilling 2026-10-19):
- `Defk.Examples.Result`, a struct at dev/defk/examples/result.ex: `decode/1` (the JSON line in), `reused?/1`, `quiet?/1`, `provisional?/1`, `rank/1`, `mark/1`, and the fields the scoreboard reads. Scoreboard, snapshot, tables and the task call predicates instead of indexing keys.
- `Defk.Bench` keeps the verdict bands (it decides the verdict, ADR-0011) and writes the line from one function.
- ADR-0011 stands: the line stays in Bench, the cache in dev.

Tests: rank and mark get one test; scoreboard_doc_test and examples_task_test exercise the record. Gate: `mix ci`; PR per AGENTS.md; no example is re-measured.

comments.text: PR #64: Defk.Examples.Result; one DEFK_RESULT writer in Bench; tables byte-identical; mix ci green (2294 passed).

title: Defk.Examples.Result: the example result is one record, not thirty string keys
